messages:
marc: FYI - L4 latency regression on long-decoder workloads after runtime v2.3.1. Seems to be falling back to `generic_attn` on certain SMs that don't expose fused_tiled_attn. Logs below.

marc: ```
[2026-03-20T15:02:11Z] model=opt-30b seq=2048 kernel=generic_attn SM=sm_l4 cap=0x4 p99=312ms -> expected ~90ms
```
anya: Do we know which exact capability bit is flipping? Can you dump DeviceFeatureMask from the probe? :eyes:

kevin: I ran a probe locally against a few L4 boxes; mask shows `0x4` (no tiled_attn) but A100/H100 show `0x1|0x2` on the same driver. Suspect probe path hits an alignment/tiling check for seq>1024 and marks tiled_attn unsupported (false negative).

tess: If that's true we should not break the kernel selection API. Suggest adding a "soft-flag" where selector returns a confidence score + fallback cost so the orchestrator can decide routing instead of a hard gate.

kevin: Rough proposal: KernelSelectorV2 returns (preferred_kernel, confidence: 0-1, fallback_cost_tokens_per_ms). Runtime keeps backward-compatible behavior when confidence<0.5. Config example: 

```
kernel_selector:
  enable_v2: true
  soft_gate_threshold: 0.5
```

kevin: Benefits: 1) allows routing decisions (send high-confidence fused_tiled_attn to A100/H100 pools), 2) avoids noisy false negatives on L4, 3) surfaces telemetry for automated rollouts.

marc: We'll need telemetry keys: `kernel_choice`, `capability_mask`, `confidence`, `fallback_cost`. Also a guardrail so private deploys can opt-out.

runtime-bot: deploy v2.3.2-canary started on cluster 'staging-gpu-l4' (canary=10%). :rocket:

anya: Two concrete follow-ups: 1) add microbench CI for seq in [1024,4096] across all GPU families; 2) define probe handshake semantics: run tiled_attn microkernel with a tiny golden output check to avoid false negatives.

kevin: I'll draft an RFC that includes the KernelSelectorV2 API, telemetry fields, and a rollout plan with a canary gating metric (p99 latency delta & regression rate). Will ping infra for a maintenance window.

tess: +1. Also make selector pluggable at the device-adapter boundary so enterprises can replace/disable it in Private deploys.

marc: Nice. If anyone hits this locally DM me perf traces and the probe dump; I'll attach them to the RFC. :thumbsup:
